title: N-Queens
keyIdea: Place one queen per column, left to right. In a column try each row; it is safe if its row, its col − row diagonal and its row + col diagonal are all free (three maps, O(1) checks). Place, mark, recurse on the next column, then unmark (backtrack).

approaches.name: Scan the board in isSafe
approaches.idea: One queen per row; isSafe walks up the column and both upward diagonals.
approaches.why: Each safety check scans up to O(n) squares.

approaches.name: Row / diagonal maps (O(1) checks)
approaches.idea: rowCheck[row], upperLeft[col − row], bottomLeft[row + col] say what is taken; mark on place, unmark on backtrack.
approaches.why: Each check is three lookups; the search tries at most n · (n − 1) · … placements.

quiz.q: Why is col − row the same along a ↘ diagonal?
options: Both row and col go up by 1 each step, so their difference stays constant

quiz.q: Why is row + col the same along a ↗ diagonal?
options: row goes down by 1 as col goes up by 1, so the sum stays constant

quiz.q: Why doesn't isSafe check the column?
options: Each call fills exactly one column, so it never has two queens
